text:
maria: Quick sync: RFC follow-up about a tight contract between matchmaker and decider. I want a practical migration plan that minimizes perf regressions and keeps auditability.

tony: +1. High level concerns: rule compilation/versioning, where tenant overrides live, and how we surface why a route was chosen.

linda: I'd like us to consider a two-tier evaluation model: compile-time -> produce a compact evaluation graph; runtime -> evaluate graph with bounded ops. Keeps DSL expressivity but makes hot path bounded.

maria: That's basically my mental model. Compiler emits a small vector of numeric scores and a few flags. matchmaker reads vector, makes quick cut. decider replays full graph for ties or overrides.

sam: Practical worry: what happens when a new rule is deployed that changes the graph shape? matchmaker caches preflight vectors by graph-id; cache invalidation could be hairy during rollout.

linda: Proposal: graph-id = (policy-version, compile-hash). matchmaker keeps entries keyed by graph-id. During rollout we stream a graph update event that includes next_graph_id and a hot-swap window. We keep both until TTL.

ton y: (typo) tony: Also need to support progressive rollout semantics for policies: allow canary tenants to use the new graph while others stay on old one. That aligns with standard feature-flag gating.

maria: Agree. Also think about safety: decider should always be able to validate matchmaker's decision. If mismatch, decider overrides and logs. Need strong telemetry.

ops-bot: policy-audit-bot: new schema required: add fields decision_graph_id, preflight_vector, final_vector, matchmaker_graph_id, divergence_flag.

sam: On runtime cost: we should limit the vector size to fixed-length (e.g., 8 floats) and cap eval ops to N. Otherwise someone could write an expensive predicate that blows up CPU.

linda: We can compile predicates to an opcode set and reject expressions that exceed the opcode budget during compile. Also reject any user-facing constructs that require non-deterministic or external I/O at eval-time.

ton y: For tenant overrides (emergency SLA or admin pin): where to evaluate? If we keep authoritative overrides in decider, we avoid divergence but add extra tail. If matchmaker applies lightweight override, we risk inconsistency.

maria: My take: authoritative overlay lives in decider. Allow matchmaker to apply a permissive shadow overlay only for healthfast path, but never to route without decider confirmation. Shadow overlay should be signed with graph-id so decider can detect misuse.

sam: That means matchmaker must attach a preflight_signature and timestamp. Decider verifies signature and checks TTL. If expired or signature mismatch, decider ignores preflight for final. We log anomalies.

linda: Another optimization: materialize heavy-weight predicates offline. e.g., affinity scores that require historical telemetry can be precomputed per instance and injected into the graph as static inputs. matchmaker then reads them cheaply.

ton y: Good call. We should standardize a small set of external inputs (e.g., recent_latency_p95, cost_per_token_est, warm_score) that are updated every Xs. That avoids per-request lookups.

maria: On observability: decision explanation must be reproducible. We need a stable explain API that, given decision_graph_id and inputs, can replay and produce an ordered trace. Keep the trace bounded to avoid huge logs.

sam: Don't forget rollout constraints: migration steps: 1) compile-only mode where entries are produced but not consumed (shadow), 2) enable matchmaker to read new vectors for canaries, 3) expand to 25/50/100% with monitoring gates, 4) final cutover.

linda: And rollback criteria: any p95 increase >3%, divergence rate >0.5% of routed requests, or fallback-to-safe-route rate >1% should auto-flag.

ton y: We need automated sanity checks in the compiler: policy linter that warns about non-idempotent constructs, heavy-cost ops, and use of tenant-unscoped globals. Ship lint failures as blocking for deploy.

maria: Ops-wise: add a short circuit path in matchmaker to avoid RPCs to decider when cluster-wide load is high. Decision: prefer regional affinity then cheapest tier. Documented and test-covered.

sam: ops-bot: rollout plan registered -> https://internal/rfc/graph-contract/migration/4419991234. Canary tenants: infra-canary-1, partner-canary-9.

ops-bot: metric-bot: canary metrics -> 6h: p95 +0.9%, divergence rate 0.12%, fallback rate 0.02%.

linda: Looks good so far. One last thing: versioning semantics. If policy DSL semantics change in a non-backwards-compatible way we must bump major policy-version and require explicit tenant opt-in. No silent rewrites.

maria: Agreed. I'll write the migration playbook and include the compiler budget rules, signature format for preflight, and the telemetry schema. Expect a PR by EOD tomorrow.

ton y: I'll add compiler-lint rules to the repo and a unit test harness for graph replay.

sam: I'll add infra bench jobs to verify budgeted eval times at 0/10k/100k qps. also add chaos test for decider unavailability.

maria: Thanks all. If nothing else, we'll merge the follow-up doc after the PRs land and start canaries next week.
